standard_prerequisites.name: Weighted arc families, their alpha weights and the Sullivan-type condition
standard_prerequisites.statement: An element of the open/closed Sullivan space wSull(n_1,n_2,m_1,m_2) is a projectivized (PMC) orbit of an arc family on a brane-labelled windowed surface whose arcs run from incoming to outgoing windows; the alpha weight of a window is the sum of the weights of the arcs incident to it.
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: the article's own review of the model at source lines 250-475, in particular the arc-family and Sullivan conventions
standard_prerequisites.use: Only the notion of the weight of a window, of an arc graph of Sullivan type and of the PMC action is assumed; the cell decomposition, the retraction and the cellularity of the gluings are the retained obligations.

standard_prerequisites.name: Standard cell-complex language: cells, interiors of cells, deformation retraction, cellular maps
standard_prerequisites.statement: A CW complex is a Hausdorff space with a filtration by closed cells whose interiors are disjoint open cells and whose attaching maps land in lower skeleta; a deformation retraction is a homotopy from the identity to a retraction fixing the subspace.
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: standard topology; used at source lines 1583-1605
standard_prerequisites.use: The vocabulary in which the proposition is stated. The author's argument that the subspace really carries such a structure, with the stated cells and attaching maps, is retained in full.

standard_prerequisites.name: Cell operad model for the closed sector of the same author's earlier work
standard_prerequisites.statement: The cellular chains of the closed analogue form a PROP cell model, and the associativity of the cellular gluing maps on the nose is established there.
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: cited by the author as [hoch1, Theorem 5.33] at source line 1607; the entry is carried in the bibliography supplied with this excerpt
standard_prerequisites.use: This is a pointer to the closed half of the argument that the author transfers; the open half, where punctures are kept and the boundary twist condition is absent, is the retained obligation (source lines 1607-1610).

core_obligations: Show that Sull_1(n_1,n_2,m_1,m_2), the subspace of wSull(n_1,n_2,m_1,m_2) on which the alpha weight of every incoming window equals one, is a deformation retract of the whole space, by the flow that scales the weights of the arcs incident to an incoming window w by the factor 1 - t(1/alpha(w) - 1) (source lines 1582-1584, with the defining context at lines 1568-1573).

Build the cell decomposition before passing to PMC orbits: for a fixed Sullivan type the weighted graphs form a product of simplices, one factor per incoming window, and after quotienting by the PMC action one obtains a cell C(Gamma) whose interior is the product of the open simplices Delta^{|{arcs incident to w}|} over the incoming windows w (source lines 1586-1597).

Identify the attaching maps with the boundary operation that deletes an arc in the limit where its weight tends to zero, and prove that the gluing maps are cellular because gluing a window with n arcs to a window with m arcs produces at most n + m - 1 arcs (source lines 1598-1605).

Prove that these cellular gluing maps are associative on the nose, transferring the closed part of the argument from the cited cell-operad theorem and treating the open part separately, where the punctures are kept on gluing and the boundary twist condition does not arise (source lines 1607-1610).

Conclude the remaining two assertions of the statement: that Sull_1 is a CW complex with the cells C(Gamma) indexed by Sullivan-type arc graphs with k + 1 arcs in dimension k, and that the condition 'every incoming window has weight one' is preserved by gluing so that Sull_1 is a sub-topological quasi-PROP (source lines 1576-1579, 1601-1602).
proof_roadmap: Define the flow that normalises the weights of the arcs incident to incoming windows and conclude that Sull_1 is a deformation retract of wSull.

Before taking PMC orbits, enumerate the arcs of a graph of Sullivan type along the incoming windows and identify the weighted graphs of that type with a product of simplices; note that the PMC action has no isotropy inside this product but may identify sides.

For each arc graph Gamma of Sullivan type on a brane-labelled windowed surface F, form the cell C(Gamma) with interior the product of open simplices over the incoming windows, and read the attaching maps off from the topology of wSull, where deleting an arc is the limit of a vanishing weight.
Check that normalised weight is stable under gluing and that gluing two windows with n and m arcs yields at most n + m - 1 arcs, so the gluing maps are cellular and descend to the cellular level.
Establish associativity on the nose of the cellular gluing maps: the closed case is the cited cell-operad theorem, and the open case is simpler because punctures are kept on gluing.
Conclude that the cellular chains of Sull_1 form the announced cell model, which the immediately following Theorem 6.4 records as a corollary; that theorem is not part of the counted statement here.
difficulty_reason: The proposition asserts three things at once about the subspace Sull_1 of the weighted open/closed Sullivan space on which every incoming window has weight one: that it is a CW complex, that it is a sub-topological quasi-PROP, and that it is a deformation retract of the full Sullivan space, with k-cells indexed by Sullivan-type arc graphs with k + 1 arcs and attaching maps given by deleting arcs. The proof has to construct the cell decomposition before passing to PMC orbits, because only then do the weighted graphs of a fixed Sullivan type form a product of simplices whose sides may still be identified by the action, giving cells C(Gamma) with interiors the products of open simplices Delta^{|{arcs incident to w}|} over the incoming windows w (source lines 1586-1597). The step that cannot be done routinely is the associativity on the nose of the induced cellular gluing maps: the author transfers it from the closed case of the cited cell-operad theorem and then argues the open case separately, since gluing keeps the punctures and the 'twisted at the boundary' condition of the closed case does not arise (source lines 1607-1610).

dedup.scope: Targeted neighbours only: every public item whose record mentions this DOI, the open/closed Sullivan spaces, arc graphs, PROPs and operads of arc families, string topology or Hochschild complexes, plus the retired-claims list and the preparation worklist, and the same-source counted unit. compared: public 2757 (same source, counted unit): Theorem 5.1 with label discretethm, statement source lines 1249-1254, proofs at 1261-1263 and 1267-1412. It states that the discrete arc-graph correlators define an action respecting every window gluing for basic ordinary Frobenius systems satisfying conditions C and E. That is a statement about correlators and gluings; it says nothing about a CW structure, about cells indexed by arc graphs, about attaching maps, or about a deformation retraction, and none of its counted spans overlaps this task's spans (1575-1580, 1582-1611, 1568-1573).

public 1432 (doi:10.3842/SIGMA.2021.086, label theo11) and public 2039 (doi:10.5802/jep.142, theorem 1): operadic constructions on typed trees and on Loday realizations of associahedra.
